thesis: The world's largest gold miner is printing record free cash flow ($3.1B in Q1 alone) at $4,100/oz gold, yet trades ~31% below the $139 street consensus after the bullion correction — the pullback is the entry.
markdown:
## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
**BUY** with $130 price target (+36.4% from $95.34, as of 7/10/26) over 12 months. Gold's correction from January's $5,597/oz record to ~$4,104/oz has knocked NEM well off its 52-week high ($134.88), but the cash-flow math barely moved: with large-cap AISC at $1,400–1,600/oz, Newmont still operates at historically extreme margins and generated an all-time record $3.1B of free cash flow in Q1 2026. Consensus (22 analysts, Buy) sits at $139; Jefferies set $146 on July 6. Central-bank demand and geopolitical fragmentation keep the structural gold bid intact.

## FUNDAMENTAL ANALYSIS
**Recent Financial Metrics**: Q1 2026 — ~1.3M attributable gold ounces produced and a record $3.1B quarterly free cash flow. FY2025 revenue $22.67B (+21.3% YoY vs $18.68B), with earnings up 111.6%. Market cap ~$101.8B; 52-week range $55.37–$134.88.

**Margin math**: At ~$4,100/oz spot versus $1,400–1,600/oz all-in sustaining costs, gross cash margins exceed $2,500/oz — levels that were unimaginable two years ago and that persist even after a further correction toward $3,500.

**Peer Comparison**: NEM is the largest gold producer, ahead of Agnico Eagle and Barrick; all three carry similar AISC bands, but Newmont's scale, Tier-1 asset concentration, and post-Newcrest portfolio rationalization (divestment proceeds funding buybacks) differentiate the capital-return story.

**Forward Outlook**: Street expects sustainable free cash flow supported by higher incremental production; the swing variable is bullion, not operations.

## CATALYST ANALYSIS
**Near-term (0–6 months)**: Q2 2026 earnings (late July) — FCF run-rate and buyback pace at ~$4,100/oz gold; further central-bank purchase data; Fed path (real rates are gold's key macro input).
**Medium-term (6–24 months)**: Continued portfolio high-grading, capital returns scaling with the FCF record, potential re-rating of gold equities toward bullion (miners have lagged the metal through the rally).
**Event-driven**: Sector M&A — record margins historically trigger consolidation; NEM is the natural consolidator.

## VALUATION & PRICE TARGETS
Consensus (S&P Global, 22 analysts): Buy, average target $139.04. Jefferies $146 (7/6/26); CIBC Outperform, target trimmed to $175 on Q1 cost outlook (still the street high tracked). LIQD base case $130 assumes gold stabilizes in a $3,800–4,400 band. Bull case $150 on a retest toward $5,000. Bear case $75 if the correction extends below $3,200 and margin compression compounds with cost inflation. Probability weighting: 25%/55%/20%.

## RISK ASSESSMENT
**Company risks**: Cost inflation (the driver of CIBC's target trim), execution across a large multi-jurisdiction portfolio, mine-sequencing and grade variability.
**Macro risks**: Gold price — a sharp rally in real yields or USD is the primary bear case; the metal has already corrected ~27% from its January record, which mitigates but does not eliminate downside.
**Position sizing**: 2–4%; gold equity beta to bullion runs ~2x, so NEM also functions as a portfolio hedge against the geopolitical scenarios that hurt industrial metals.

## TECHNICAL CONTEXT & OPTIONS INTELLIGENCE
$95.34 sits in the lower half of the $55.37–$134.88 52-week range after the bullion-led pullback from the high. The $134.88 high marks long-term resistance; the pre-rally consolidation zone in the $80s is first support. Options flow data not sourced in this run — n/a.

## MARKET POSITIONING
Gold equities lagged bullion through the 2025–26 rally, and generalist ownership remains light — the setup that historically precedes miner re-ratings. Within the LIQD Metals framework NEM is the quality-gold allocation alongside copper-first positioning (see METALS sector note, 7/13/26).

## INSIDER SIGNALS
Insider transaction data not sourced in this run — n/a. Capital-return signal: management has directed record FCF toward buybacks and the base dividend.
